title: Gaskiers glaciation
summary: The Gaskiers glaciation, dated to about 580 million years ago, is best preserved in rocks of the Avalon Peninsula in eastern Newfoundland, Canada, with a correlative unit on the Bonavista Peninsula. It is usually described as short-lived and confined to the Gaskiers Formation, but recent work argues the onset was gradual, with the underlying Mall Bay Formation dated to about 608 to 580 Ma. Ediacaran fossils occur beneath the Bonavista equivalent.

uncertainty.note: Three opened pages give ca. 580 Ma (Fitzgerald thesis, Liu and Tindal, Gomez et al. EGU abstract); Hannah et al. (AGU 2014) state that the type Gaskiers units are 582 to 584 Ma from ash-bed dating. The glaciation is treated here as a single date because the pages do not give start and end. Years are Ma counted back from the present with no 1950 offset.
